key_insight: Use one offline adjoint sensitivity analysis to weight Reynolds-stress training data by their impact on a target quantity of interest, rather than treating all stress errors equally.
engineering_relevance: This improves RANS turbulence-model learning for complex flows by better aligning supervised training with downstream engineering predictions while avoiding repeated expensive flow solves.
method: Compute local sensitivities of the chosen QoI to each Reynolds-stress component with a single offline adjoint evaluation.
Convert those sensitivities into fixed weights in the supervised loss for Reynolds-stress learning.
Train the turbulence constitutive model with goal-oriented weights, without further RANS solves during optimization.
evidence_signal: The approach was validated on square-duct and periodic-hill flows and then on a film-cooling jet in crossflow, where it improved velocity and cooling-effectiveness predictions versus uniform weighting.
watch_item: The weighting depends on the chosen QoI and the quality of the offline adjoint sensitivity estimate, so mismatched objectives or inaccurate sensitivities can limit gains.
paper_title: Goal-Oriented Weighting of Reynolds-Stress Data for Learning Turbulence Models in Complex Flows
